$schema-note: Declarative context→agent mapping. The mapper (bin/lib/context-map.mjs) reads this and (re)writes the `resources` array of each .kiro/agents/<agent>.json. Shared-root entries (context/*, openspec, sdlc.config.json, pipelines.json) resolve to the project root (file://./<entry>, no symlink); platform-local entries (steering, ai) resolve under .kiro/ (file://./.kiro/<entry>). extraDocs are project-root-relative. Any path is SKIPPED if it does not exist — so the kit never produces a broken reference. Edit this file (or let the onboarder agent edit it), then run the mapper.
$cost-note: knowledgeBase entries are RAG-indexed (indexType: best), so a broad source costs retrieval noise, not fixed per-spawn tokens — but noise is worse than cost: a chunk from an ARCHIVED change reads as current spec. So the openspec kb is scoped to `openspec/specs` (the living capability specs) + `openspec/config.yaml`; `openspec/changes/**` is NEVER indexed — a role reads the ACTIVE change by explicit path (every role prompt already names it). `steering` is not listed here either: Kiro auto-includes .kiro/steering/*.md by front-matter `inclusion`, so indexing it too would double-count it.

extraDocs.$comment: Optional project-specific doc paths (relative to project root, e.g. "docs/30-architecture"). Add per-agent arrays to append extra knowledgeBase sources without editing .json by hand.
